en: The *Dacheng ke xu* (Preface to the Great Perfection) of the *Lotus Sūtra* has become the standard for the age. Among the young and the beginners, there are none who do not find their hearts intoxicated by it;

even among the venerable elders who expound upon it, all follow its strict guidelines, for it exhaustively elucidates the source of the principles of all Buddhas and gathers together [the essence of] the multitude.
The terminology of this work is also that of the *Jia* (Family) school. This commentary was begun by the Venerable Master Banweng;

its topical headings (*kemu*) are all orderly and systematic. However, as there is no separate manual for quick reference, those of venerable seniority face the trouble of turning through many pages, while beginners are not without the risk of falling into confusion.
My elder brother Yuanliang was concerned about this matter; therefore, during his leisure from lecturing, he labored...

It has been compiled into a formal volume so that students and commentators may view it as clearly as seeing something on the palm of their hand, thereby perhaps avoiding the cumbersome errors mentioned above.
Having completed the work, he commissioned me to write a preface. I considered my own lack of literary talent and dared not append words;

yet, I shall briefly describe its benefits for the convenience of the young in their advancement and for the benefit of the elderly in virtue. It is not only a precursor star to the Great Achievement (Dacheng), but also serves as a guide for the Half-Elder (Banweng).
Is this not a meritorious achievement?
